classification.difficultyReason: The student translates square-base volume into a cubic, selects factorisation procedures and interprets the real root as positive box dimensions.

content.prompt: A box has a square base of side length $x$ cm and a height that is 3 cm less than the length of the base. The volume of the box is $50\text{ cm}^3$. Write a polynomial equation modelling this scenario and hence find the dimensions of the box.

answer.short: $x^3-3x^2-50=0$; the box is $5\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
The base has side length $x$ cm and the height is $(x-3)$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}x^2(x-3)&=50\\x^3-3x^2&=50\\x^3-3x^2-50&=0\end{align*}$$
Let $P(x)=x^3-3x^2-50$. Test factors of $50$:
$$P(5)=125-75-50=0.$$
Therefore $x-5$ is a factor. Long division, with the missing $x$ term shown as $0x$, gives
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2+2x+10\\\hline x-5&x^3-3x^2+0x-50\\&\underline{-(x^3-5x^2)}\\&2x^2+0x-50\\&\underline{-(2x^2-10x)}\\&10x-50\\&\underline{-(10x-50)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Hence
$$(x-5)(x^2+2x+10)=0.$$
The quadratic has discriminant $2^2-4(1)(10)=-36<0$, so its roots are not real. Hence $x=5$ cm and the height is $x-3=2$ cm. The box dimensions are $5\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.
